records.title: A 5th Grader's Big Question
records.author: Gary Ricke
records.description: Pastor Tony visits a fifth-grade class to address the difficult question of why Satan still causes chaos despite Christ's victory on the cross, explaining that while Jesus definitively won the war, a defeated Satan "still rages" and tries to recruit followers on earth before his final ultimate defeat.

records.title: God’s Kindness in the Dead-Still Season
records.author: Gary Ricke
records.description: Even when your faith feels “dead still,” God’s perfect plan—relationship grounded in grace—holds firm, and His kindness (remembered especially through baptism) gently leads you to turn back toward His warmth.

records.title: Living in God's Perfect Plan: A Message from the Trees
records.author: Gary Ricke
records.description: Pastor Tony reflects on a profound question about God's will, using the simple metaphor of trees in a forest to reveal that living in God's perfect plan isn't about what we do, but about who we are as His children.

records.title: From Brokenness to Hope: Wendy's Journey of Healing and Faith
records.author: Gary Ricke
records.description: In this episode, Wendy, a participant in the "Healing the Wounds of Trauma" training, shares how confronting her pain through faith, scripture, and community support allowed her to find hope, healing, and a renewed commitment to help others.

records.title: Anchorage Lutheran Church
records.author: Gary Ricke

records.title: Healing The Wounds of Trauma: Stories of Faith and Resilience
records.author: Gary Ricke
records.description: In this podcast episode, attendees of LIM's Healing the Wounds of Trauma share how a faith has empowered them to heal personally, deepen their faith, and equip them to help their people.

records.title: Restoring Years in Marriage by Building a Strong Relationship with Christ
records.author: Gary Ricke
records.description: In this episode, Tanya Dolchok discusses her deeply personal and transformative journey with Christ, reflecting on overcoming family turmoil, maintaining a long marriage, and finding guidance and solace in her faith during the various seasons of her life.

records.title: Community Healing Through Scripture: A Journey in Copper Center, Alaska

records.title: Event: Katherine Gottlieb: “His Hands Upon Me”

records.title: TRUTH: what the world needs - Week 7 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Which truth will we believe?  God's Transcendent Truth has been revealed in the Sacred Word of God, which never changes! And by the grace of God, we come to believe in the truth of God and trust in Jesus as Lord and Savior. This is news that sounds too good to be true, but it is in fact true.

records.title: TRUTH: what the world needs - Week 6 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: For those of us who take God at his Word, we must humbly admit that this is the blessed work of Holy Spirit! To God be all glory and praise. You see, we did not choose God, we do not play a role in our being redeemed from our sin and rebellious ways. It is solely by the will and the grace and the work of God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

records.title: TRUTH: what the world needs - Week 5 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In our world, many would say truth is relative. In other words, what is true for you may not be true for me. I would counter that when truth is said to be relative by an individual, that individual would not know Truth if it were standing right in front of him.

records.title: TRUTH: what the world needs - Week 4 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: So where does one turn to for the Truth?  We turn to our Creator, His Son, and the Spirit of Truth. In other words, Transcendent Truth comes solely from one source: God - Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.  And where does one learn what God has to say?  One turns to God's Sacred Word.

records.title: TRUTH: what the world needs - Week 3 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Who do we believe today? There are so many conflicting points of view and slanted 'facts' and distorted news stories. World views and the various perspectives of people have been in conflict since the fall of mankind for the lies of Satan.  But, I have good news for you today. There is One whom you can trust and who only speaks the truth: Jesus.

records.title: TRUTH: what the world needs - Week 2 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: One of the truths Christians profess, which we just celebrated and is fresh in our minds, is of the virgin birth of God's Son, Jesus.  In the words of the Apostles' Creed, we profess Jesus   "was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary."   In the Nicene Creed, we profess Jesus  "   was incarnate by the Holy Spirit of the virgin Mary and was made man;"   And in the Athanasian Creed, we profess Jesus is God,   "begotten from the substance of the Father before all ages; and He is man, born from the substance of His mother in this age."    The virgin birth of baby Jesus, celebrated on Christmas Day, has been brought into question by non-believers around the world. We turn to God's Sacred Word as our source of Transcendent Truth.

records.title: TRUTH: what the world needs - Week 1 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We search for transcendent truth, not transient. Transient truth is what mankind comes to think and observe as true. However, over time, transient truth, through advances in technology, may be proven untrue. I will offer one example: for decades, Pluto was considered a planet. Now it is not.

records.title: Peace in the New Year - Friday, January 1 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As we celebrate the beginning of a new year, we pray the Prince of Peace would bless you with safety, wellness, and a completeness that can only come from Him.

records.title: The Star - Thursday, December 31 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: During this Christmas Season, ask God to open your heart to see the many ways He is speaking to you. He is speaking to you through the Christmas story, as well as through your surroundings. He beckons you through his creation. The Psalmist says, “The heavens declare his glory.”  God can still use the stars in the night sky to direct and lead us to Jesus, to remind us of his eternal hope, just like he did over two thousand years ago.

records.title: Time - Wednesday, December 30 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: People have their ideas, thoughts, beliefs, traditions, and way of life.  It takes time, to have discussions. It takes effort to help those in need. It takes time.  As we go out and meet needs, whether it is in your own home or in a distant country, we are examples to others of who Christ is.

records.title: Be a Follower - Tuesday, December 29 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When I began doing women’s ministry, I balked at the idea of leading other women. But then I realized, I am no leader - I am a follower. I am not leading these girls on campus. I am following a God who knows the beginning from the end. He knows the words of my mouth, their mouths, the meditations of our hearts, and  He will lead .

records.title: Recognizing Christ - Monday, December 28 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Even those of us who know Him by His grace are prone to honor our own efforts. Some people may say, “I’ve been a Christian for forty years.” Unwittingly, they may have done the same thing over and over forty times. Jesus is cajoling us every day to recognize Him in our life. He needs for us to be different.  He is calling us to grow, to change. Christmas is a time of new beginnings. Joy to the world!

records.title: Everlasting Father - Saturday, December 26 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The baby we celebrated yesterday is also the Everlasting Father, the Creator of the Heavens and the Earth, who existed at the beginning and will be forever.

records.title: This Week in Native American News (12/25/2020): Merry Christmas!
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (12/25/2020): Merry Christmas!

records.title: Fingerprints - Friday, December 25 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When I hear the Christmas story of Jesus’ birth to Mary in the stable, I also think about our own design and creation. I am in awe that God would send His Son to be born of a virgin, with his own unique body, complete with individual fingerprints! Equally awe-inspiring is the fact that Jesus would live his life and die with us in mind. Absolutely amazing- our God loves, creates, redeems, and gives a purpose to each one of us through Christ. Now that is something to celebrate this Christmas morning!

records.title: Thy Kingdom Come - Thursday, December 24 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: These three words have power: Thy kingdom come - 1) to me, 2) to others, 3) to others through me, and finally, 4) quickly - I am ready to go, through faith in Jesus, my Lord and Savior!

records.title: Mountains - Wednesday, December 23 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The mountains in this part of the world are truly awesome, and they do reflect God’s glory in creation. But what can creation do to save us? Thank God he not only shows us his power, but also his love. Jesus began the reign of peace, the time that Isaiah spoke about as the “last days.” While Jesus did gather people to himself, he also sent his disciples into the world, and still sends his disciples today.  The pattern remains: gathering people to hear God’s Word and sending them out.  To whom is God sending you today? Who do you know that needs to hear of the LORD and his mercy?

records.title: God's Whisper - Tuesday, December 22 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As I look back on my life, I can see, over and over, all God saw me through. And the greatest gift and promise of all, Jesus, reminds me of this again and again.

records.title: Loose him & let him go - Monday, December 21 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Jesus gave life back to Lazarus. Lazarus came out of the tomb still wrapped in grave clothes. Jesus said to those nearby, "Loose him and let him go." I see our team as members of that crowd gathering around Jesus. He has given life back to Native men and women, and now we get to help them remove their grave clothes, their trauma and shame, so they can live life with Jesus, free and at peace.

records.title: Mighty God - Saturday, December 19 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We have the valiant champion, the strongest power, the Almighty on our side. As we get closer to Christmas Day, let us continue to remember who it is we are celebrating. It is not merely a baby in a manger, but the Savior himself in the flesh.

records.title: This Week in Native American News (12/18/2020): Suicide Prevention, Homeless Shelters, and Traditional Celebrations
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (12/18/2020): Suicide Prevention, Homeless Shelters, and Traditional Celebrations

records.title: Identity - Friday, December 18 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Jesus would come from Bethlehem, the house of bread, and the tribe of Judah. His mother would be Mary and His Father Yahweh in heaven. His name would denote His contribution to His people. Jesus, for He will save His people through the forgiveness of their sins.  As we await the second advent of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, let us remember that it is always more important to remember our identity is where we have come from, not what we have done.

records.title: Family Gatherings - Thursday, December 17 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: There is one other family gathering that most choose to not attend. Each and every week the family of God, brothers and sisters in Christ, gather at one of God's houses. Creator God invites and welcomes one and all to gather together in order that they might receive good gifts from Him!  These gifts are offered at no cost to those who come. As a matter of fact, it cost Creator God His One and Only Son's life in order to keep the welcome mat out for you forever. You are invited to give to God, as a goodwill offering: your sorrow for His joy, your weakness for His strength, your sin for His righteousness.

records.title: Shine His Light
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Some 2,000 years ago, God sent his Son. He became man to shine His light into a dark and hurting world.  Today, Christ shines His light through individuals - people like you and me, people like the staff of Lutheran Indian Ministries. We have been given the opportunity to serve our Native brothers and sisters, to help them find the Light and the hope in the midst of darkness.

records.title: Light of the World - Wednesday, December 16 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: May each of us be renewed this Advent season with a physical sense of joy and wonder. Like those of us in Fairbanks, and the northern villages, seeing a full day of sunshine after a very long winter, let us feel a physical sense of relief, as we remember that the light of the world has come down to us and redeems us. And let us bring that Light into every aspect of our lives to share it with those still living in darkness.

records.title: Why are you here? - Tuesday, December 15 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: How did you get here? And why are you here? The answer to these two questions is simple. Because of Jesus!  Just like Sunday school, the answer is always Jesus.

records.title: The Final Word - Monday, December 14 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Reading Micah’s prophecies is a challenge of endurance. Back and forth like a divine pendulum, the prophet alternates harsh words of condemnation for God’s rebellious children to tender appeals of comfort and restoration. It leaves the reader asking: Which is it? Mercy or wrath? Pardon or punishment?

records.title: Wonderful Counselor - Saturday, December 12 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In hope and trust, we turn to Jesus, our Wonderful Counselor.  Like a worldly counselor, he is available to advise and help us work out problems and feelings that may arise during the holiday season.  Unlike the human counselor, his answers and guidance, found in the Word, are extraordinary and perfect.

records.title: The Promise of Hope - Friday, December 11 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Advent is the season of waiting and looking forward to a celebration. Essentially, it is all about hope.  While hope is, generally, forward-focused, it can also mean looking back. Especially around Advent, we reflect on the goodness we have already received - the Savior born in the manger who died, was buried, and rose again - and let it help us to anticipate what is still to come - Jesus' mighty return.

records.title: Let my people go - Thursday, December 10 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: So, God sayeth: "Go down, Moses Way down in Egypt land Tell all Pharaohs to Let my people go"  We must be there to help our Native brothers and sisters find deliverance from the bondage of their past trauma and pain, so they can worship the Lord!

records.title: December Update from Sacred Ground - Haskell
records.author: Guest User

records.title: Our Daily Bread
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As Lutheran Indian Ministries moves into the new year, our mission and focus continue to be: Proclaim. Disciple. Heal. And as we do this, we feel a special urgency when it comes to healing trauma and addiction in order to help our Native brothers and sisters experience the joy of God’s peace, bodily health, and faithful, Christian friends and mentors.

records.title: Eternal Father - Wednesday, December 9 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Jesus, the Son, in His humanity, showed the physical expression of the deep love the Father has for all humanity, including you and me. Jesus is the embodiment of this love. “For God so loved the world that he sent his only begotten Son, that whosoever believes in Him will have eternal life.” (John 3:16)

records.title: I Can't Even Walk - Tuesday, December 8 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Our world is going through troubling times. I have no idea what you may be going through this Christmas. But I do know one thing:  Because Jesus came, there is hope.

records.title: God sees the potential - Monday, December 7 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: God sees the potential; we trust him and help to begin the restoring and renovating process. There are hiccups along the way, minor repairs, easy patches, big tear downs, projects that seem to last for a long time, and projects that come together miraculously. You really feel like progress is being made and then WHAM, sewage backs up and you take several steps back. You wonder why you even started, but you roll up your sleeves and you (figuratively) start shoveling out the poop, wondering if you were even making progress to begin with. Months later, you are still at it and look up and realize: Wow God, you saw this masterpiece the entire time! You just asked us to be faithful. We give you the glory, God, because we didn’t see it. We saw work, steps backward, an impossible outcome but You saw the finished project.

records.title: Immanuel - Saturday, December 5 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In this time of waiting and anticipation, we are reassured that God is always with us.

records.title: This Week in Native American News (12/4/2020): National Parks, Short Films, & Supporting Native Art
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (12/4/2020): National Parks, Short Films, & Supporting Native Art

records.title: A Circle of Trust - Friday, December 4 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In the Christian faith, the circle (or ring) represents the symbol of eternity and never-ending existence, as well as the everlasting and perfect love of God. The Advent wreath, with its five candles, represents the perfect gifts we receive from our Heavenly Father: faith, hope, joy, peace, and the unending love of God.

records.title: Living in the Waiting Room - Thursday, December 3 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We wait for the Lord our God because He will reward our waiting with His gifts. Victory over sin and temptation, forgiveness that leads to eternal life, and a restored, permanent relationship with God and His promise to be with as always. But we need not spend any more time in the waiting room. It is all yours today through faith in Jesus.

records.title: Let's Go to the House of the Lord - Wednesday, December 2 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: At this time of the year, many churches offer a mid-week worship service as we anticipate Jesus’ birth and second coming. These services are often poorly attended, but our Lord invites us to accept with joy the invitation to come and worship him. God has done so many marvelous things, and when we consider all of what he has done it ought to be natural to say “Yes! Let’s go to the house of the LORD!”

records.title: The Countdown - Tuesday, December 1 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Many families use Advent calendars to help children understand the concepts of faith and patience. With their 25 little numbered doors, pockets, or drawers, children countdown from December 1st to Christmas Day. These calendars can help people, not just children, grow in their anticipation of the day when we celebrate the first arrival of our long-promised Redeemer, God’s Son, Jesus.

records.title: Blessing in Disguise - Monday, November 30 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Advent culminates at the birth of our Savior, Jesus Christ. Our blessing in disguise. This little baby born in a simple stable is actually God’s solution for our captivity to sin and the law. We are now able to focus on the new life and freedom given to us through faith in our Savior.

records.title: Comforter in You - Sunday, November 29 (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We can feel alone, even in a large family. We may feel overlooked by those we love, whether parents, siblings, or spouse. We miss those who have left us, in death or broken relationships. During the holiday season, many people struggle with depression and anxiety leaving them feeling even more alone. But we are never alone.

records.title: Advent Starts Tomorrow (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We can feel alone, even in a large family. We may feel overlooked by those we love, whether parents, siblings, or spouse. We miss those who have left us, in death or broken relationships. During the holiday season, many people struggle with depression and anxiety leaving them feeling even more alone. But we are never alone.

records.title: In anticipation... (Advent 2020)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Jesus spoke the Parable of the Sower to teach us how important the state of our heart is to receive the Gospel and how our salvation is proved by our choices and actions after hearing the Gospel.  As you read these Advent devotions, I pray the stories of our efforts to prepare and repair the hearts of Native people to receive the Gospel will inspire, uplift, and sustain you.

records.title: Ministry Prayer Requests & Thanksgiving
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Join us in prayers of Thanksgiving for our staff and the work they do in Native ministry!

records.title: Don't forget about Thanksgiving! (Monday Morning Devotion)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We can’t really experience or understand Christmas unless we first conform our hearts to the   longing   of Advent. Advent calls us all to refocus our lives on God’s promise of deliverance and the flesh-and-blood reality of Jesus Christ, our Deliverer – who came to us first in Bethlehem, comes to us today in the Eucharist, and will come again at the end of time.  Likewise, we can’t give truly good gifts with love, without first   thanking   God for the gifts he has given us. It’s always good to recognize and reflect on what we are thankful for.  It is fitting that Thanksgiving falls directly before the Advent season

records.title: Feed My Sheep
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When Jesus says, “Feed my sheep,” as Christians, we understand Jesus is telling Peter to continue His ministry, shepherding the believers, feeding them God’s Word. But there are many stories where Jesus literally fed his flock: the feeding of the 5,000, the Lord’s Supper, and right before he speaks to Peter in this story, he feeds him fish and bread.  At Lutheran Indian Ministries, we believe in the healing and restorative Word of God,  and  we understand that the physical and emotional care we can provide builds trust and opens the hearts of those who might otherwise close themselves off to knowing our loving and unchanging Heavenly Father.   We will continue to feed his sheep, spiritually and physically.

records.author: Guest User
records.description: Most of us love to remain in our comfort zones and hate surprises, especially in the land of Lutherans. We go to the same service every Sunday and sit in   our   seats. We love the old pastor, the old hymnal, and we sure miss the old organist.  Change is can be upsetting. It disrupts our “normal” and forces us to try new ways of doing things.

records.title: Living By Faith: A Time for Peace - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 8
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Maybe you drifted from God in the past months. It’s not too late. You don’t need a Stay-at-Home order to take time to turn to your Heavenly Father and spend time listening to Him.

records.title: Living By Faith: Shaken - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 7
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Life can suddenly shake. We can go to bed one night and wake the next morning to a pandemic, economic turmoil, political upheaval. It feels as though everything we have is in crisis. But that which is unshakable remains. The kingdom of God, in Christ, remains eternal. Nothing can separate us from the love of God.

records.title: Living By Faith: Just Sheep - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 6
records.author: Guest User
records.description: While I, too often, act like a sheep, it helps me to remember I am God’s sheep. And like a good shepherd, He will provide for me and guide me. He promises none of His sheep will be lost. We know Jesus’ voice. We are His sheep, and He will lead us out of trouble.

records.title: This Week in Native American News (8/28/2020): Skating, Dancing, and Name Changes

records.title: Living By Faith: Dread - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 5
records.author: Guest User
records.description: For Christians, this Psalm is even more comforting when we realize God has destroyed the enemies we could never defeat: sin, death, and the power of the devil. Salvation for God’s people has come from Zion, where Jesus cried, “It is finished!” and death lost its sting (1 Cor. 15:55). The worst that can happen to any of us is we die. But death has already been defeated. There is now nothing to dread or be afraid of.

records.title: Living By Faith - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 4
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Life is much like this passage. When we are saved by Christ, we are to cut the umbilical cord of the world, but often we are still attached to our worldly ways.

records.title: Fighting Isolation & the loss of culture
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Native people living on tribal lands are quarantining to preserve their past and ensure their future. The mission is worthy: save the lives of the elders, save the culture. But in doing so, the mental and emotional isolation is breeding more addiction and mental health issues, among other problems.

records.title: Living By Faith: Out of the World - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 3
records.author: Guest User
records.description: It is hard to not get wrapped up into worrying about our nation and the fear of destruction, but we need to understand this is not ours to worry about. This is not our kingdom.  We should, instead, look to our heavenly kingdom and our heavenly Father. God has everything under control. He is sovereign.

records.title: Living By Faith: Fear or Faith - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 2
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Science says, you cannot be driven by anxiety and live in joy; our brains just won’t allow it. God’s word reinforces this and teaches us.

records.title: Call on Me (Today's LIM)
records.author: Guest User

records.title: Living By Faith: Heroes - Monday Morning Summer Devotion Series - Week 1
records.author: Guest User
records.description: During these uncertain times, I look at how David found the strength to battle Goliath. He wasn’t a warrior, wasn’t trained, and didn’t have the right tools. He had all of the acceptable excuses to back out, yet he stood firm, trusting that his strength was from the Lord.

records.title: A New Trauma
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We heard the warnings and followed the rules: Stay home, social distance, self-quarantine for 14 days. We did our best, and we flattened curves. Yeah, us! But, what about the individuals who, because of the forced isolation, were exposed to abusive relationships, addictions, and worsening physical and mental health issues. This pandemic has made Native ministry even more relevant.

records.title: The Making of  Spiritual Warrior - Week 7 - Monday Morning Devotions
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The training to make someone into a Spiritual Warrior is not a one-time event, nor is it a program to be completed. In other words, it is not merely a matter of being baptized, nor is it having completed a confirmation class or an adult instruction program. No, it is a cyclical ongoing and lifelong endeavor.

records.title: Disturb Me: Week 7 - Monday Morning Devotions
records.author: Guest User
records.description: I had access to the Creator and Sustainer of the universe. The Great I am. The Alpha and the Omega. The Beginning and the End. The all-powerful, ever-present, all-knowing God who can send fire from heaven, shut the mouths of hungry lions, or calm a raging storm. And all I asked him to do was keep me safe and help me have a good day.  Now answer honestly. If God said yes to every prayer you prayed in the last seven days, how would the world be different?

records.author: Guest User

records.title: Break Me: Week 5 - Monday Morning Devotions
records.author: Guest User
records.description: It’s fine to pray for safety and blessings, but what if you want more? What if you desire power from the Holy Spirit, strength from heaven, unshakable faith, genuine intimacy with your Father?  Instead of just asking God to keep you safe, give you more, and protect your life, you may have to ask God to break you.

records.title: He is Risen Indeed!
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As life returns to “normal,” and we begin to gather once again to study His Word and worship, I invite you to walk with us. Not just to continue your support of Lutheran Indian Ministries with your prayers and gifts, but to do so with urgency. Help us reach Native lives as though there is no tomorrow. Let’s use these lessons we’ve learned to do God’s will more passionately and intentionally.  Satan intended our distancing for evil, but we can use it to grow God’s Kingdom as we’ve never seen before.

records.title: Reveal My Fears: Week 4 - Monday Morning Devotions
records.author: Guest User
records.description: “Lord, reveal what holds my mind hostage. Show me what I fear the most. Go ahead, help me face what terrifies me.”  What we fear matters.

records.title: Search Me: Week 3 - Monday Morning Devotions
records.author: Guest User
records.description: On the surface, it seems like we would know our own hearts. Right?  I know my motives. I know what’s most important. I know why I do what I do.  Besides, you might tell yourself,  I’ve got a good heart. I’m not trying to hurt people. I want to do what’s right. My heart is good. I’m praying, aren’t I?   But God’s Word actually reveals the exact opposite.

records.title: Your Will Be Done: Week 2 - Monday Morning Devotions
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Your prayers matter.  How you pray matters.  What you pray matters.  Your. Prayers. Move. God.

records.title: It's Time for Dangerous Prayers: Week 1 - Monday Morning Devotions
records.author: Guest User
records.description: It’s time to stop praying safe.  It’s time to start talking, really talking—and really listening—to God.  It’s time for dangerous prayers.

records.title: Praising God During a Pandemic
records.author: Guest User
records.description: God is indeed in control of all things . He will watch over you and guide you as you seek His will and His way. “And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.” (Romans 8:28)

records.title: Serving God & Sharing Hope - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Lutheran Indian Ministries is ripe with potential and opportunity. The chance to serve God and share the hope of eternal life with our Native brothers and sisters is a special one.

records.title: Live Unafraid - Lent 2020 - Happy Easter!
records.author: Guest User
records.description: If Jesus has all authority, then why am I afraid?    As the Son of God, he knew the absolute truth of what his life, death, and resurrection would accomplish.  Jesus conquered death, and therefore we can live unafraid.

records.title: Take Heart - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We are a bit spoiled. We know how this story ends. We know that Christ rises from the dead, the Holy Spirit is sent, and Christ promises to return yet again. Knowing the ending can be a great comfort. The assurance of God’s grace and our ability to come to God the Father because of Christ’s sacrifice is an unparalleled blessing.     At the same time, if we skip right to the ending, we lose some understanding of what it was like to be a follower of Christ in those uncertain days.  While Christ was with them, miracles abounded, people were healed and fed. Then, suddenly, their leader was arrested, falsely convicted, and killed. The believers were so frightened that when Christ returned, He found them hiding behind locked doors!

records.title: Forsaken So You Never Will Be - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: At times, you might have experienced the agony of being forsaken. You may have felt that no one loved you or cared about you. You might have felt neglected, taken advantage of, abused, or abandoned, maybe even by your own flesh and blood.    But in this life, you will never, ever be forsaken by Mauna.

records.title: Our Darkest Hour - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: God allows us to go through hard times. Of course, our trials are nowhere near the same as what Jesus went through on the cross, but Jesus has called us to walk through our own suffering in order to find new life in him.  In the process, do not miss that it is the hard things in life, not the easy, which teach us the most valuable lessons.  God wants to build us into people of deep and real character so we, too, can accomplish the purpose he has uniquely created for us, just as Jesus had a unique and important purpose only he could accomplish.

records.title: Do not Grieve - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In our broken and fallen world, our joy seems like this, ephemeral, brief, and transient. Not so with our LORD. His joy is our strength day in and day out.

records.title: Love as I have Loved - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: It is hard to love one another because we are sinful, selfish humans. We look at people through our human filters and often get overwhelmed by the mess in their lives. We think about the hassle and time needed to help those in need and let it get in the way of simply loving one another.    Jesus was human, too, but He didn’t let that stop Him from loving us. He didn’t turn away from our mess, he jumped right into it and joined us.

records.title: Our Sacred Work - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The work of our Sacred Ground program allows missionaries to go into communities where the door is normally shut to the church. And it is our responsibility to use that opportunity to sing our own hosannas.

records.title: Preparing for Holy Week - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As we enter the Holy Week, take time to read the passion and resurrection of Jesus in its entirety.   We recommend Matthew, which focuses on the kingship of Jesus, how the ruling powers conspired to get rid of someone they saw as a political threat.

records.title: This Week in Native American News (4/3/2020): The World Keeps Moving & So Do We
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (4/3/2020): The World Keeps Moving & So Do We

records.title: Manning the Lifeboat - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We must remember, however, that most of the world is drowning, and it is our job to reach out to those slipping under the water.  With a strong boat under our feet - the sturdy boat is the Good News of the Resurrection – we have been given the opportunity, by the power of the Holy Spirit, to help our Native brothers and sisters find the saving grace of God.

records.title: Waving in Celebration - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Let’s practice. Put on some music, sing a song, and wave your arms. Wave a branch from a tree or bush. Wave a prayer shawl. Wave some feathers. Have a joyful heart as you show God how much you appreciate His great love for you!

records.title: Love Each Other - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: How are they to love God if they cannot even love themselves?  How do we expect them to come to know a Savior who loves them, created them in His image, and sees them as His special children when they do not see themselves as any of those things?

records.title: Share the Truth - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Until they hear the truth of the Gospel of Jesus Christ, they will continue to search for the truth in false gods and worldly cures.

records.title: Sacred Ground - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: People still go to the cross of Jesus to “hunt” for the truth about salvation or find healing in their inner “sacred ground,” the soul, and it is a very real battleground as they try to live on the Jesus Path.

records.title: Joy in Sorrow - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Remember, our pain and discomfort in this world are only a small infliction before the great, everlasting glory that is to come.   More than that, we know God works for the good of those who love him. When we put our lives in his hands, he will take our weaknesses, wrongdoings, and misery and make them his own, incorporating them into His glorious plan.

records.title: This Week in Native American News (3/27/2020): Yes there is more Covid-19 news AND a great watchlist for when you are stuck in your house and bored
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (3/27/2020): Yes there is more Covid-19 news AND a great watchlist for when you are stuck in your house and bored

records.title: We are on the Way to Resurrection - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: I sometimes wonder what must have been going on in our Savior's mind as He lived His last few days on earth. He knew what was ahead of Him - the beating, the torture, the crucifixion, the weight of the sin of the world. Even though we know suffering in our own lives, this pain is something we, as humans, cannot begin to comprehend.    But Jesus also knew the end game - He was on his way to resurrection!     Knowing we are on the way to the resurrection gives us hope and courage.

records.title: While We Wait for Blessed Hope - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: People are the same the world over. And yet God loves all people.   While God loves all people, He still hates sin.  He is just and does not merely look the other way. Someone must (and already did) pay the price. Jesus, the Son of God, suffered so people of every tribe, nation, and language could seek His mercy and receive His grace.

records.title: Rend Your Hearts - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In the mysterious presence of the Christ found in his Word and Sacraments, God nurtures and sustains our faith. In the light of the Word, we see our need for a heart of repentance, and we find the strength to endure.

records.title: How Did We Get Here? - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: How did we get here? By the grace of God!  As people hear the good news of Jesus, God is still re-creating. He creates faith in Jesus out of unbelief. He gives forgiveness for our failures and life for death. In His Word, he delivers the Spirit of life and strengthens us for life in His kingdom.   Our lives have purpose and meaning. We work in the gardens in which we have been placed. We shepherd the people God has given us to live with. We seek to bless the lives of our neighbors. By God’s grace, as we journey to the foot of the cross, we see God redeeming and restoring.

records.title: Sacred Story Success at Haskell
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The weekend of Valentine’s Day saw many hearts open at Haskell LIGHT.  Our Sacred Story team converged on the Haskell Indian Nations University to touch the lives of the native students and community members by allowing them to share their stories of abuse and hurt in order to begin their healing journey.

records.title: Joy in Lent - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Yes, God’s anger is real concerning sin, but His suffering servant has canceled the power of sin.     Even in the middle of the somber reflection of Lent, there is room for joy!

records.title: Faith in the Unknown - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In today's world of self-help, putting faith in something other than your own work is called naive and ignorant. But we know all of God's works have meaning and purpose. We won't understand it all, but we find comfort in his Word and in Our Savior.

records.title: Hope for Today
records.author: Guest User

records.title: This Week in Native American News (3/20/2020): the coronavirus (of course) and the homeless, plus some Powwow rules of etiquette
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (3/20/2020): the coronavirus (of course) and the homeless, plus some Powwow rules of etiquette

records.title: My Father is With Me - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: It is comforting to know Jesus, our Savior Himself, knows what is it like to be “all alone,” particularly at a time when He most needed his friends. What a great comfort to know that we are never alone in the greatest time of our need.

records.title: Our Father's Ways - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The Bible, the inerrant Word of God, tells the story of Jesus Christ and his life spent modeling the ways of the Father.  Jesus knew His Father’s ways because the Father lived and dwelled within Him. We, too, can know the Father’s ways, through the power of the Holy Spirit, when Christ lives inside of us.

records.title: Montana Healing Project
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Because you recognize the importance of this work, LIM has been able to send our Sacred Story team to Montana twice, in the past 4 months. It is our prayer to bring Sacred Story to all seven Montana reservations. With your help, we will do that.

records.title: There is No Tomb - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: My tribe had great chiefs like Crazy Horse, Red Cloud, Sitting Bull, and Spotted Elk - all leaders we greatly respected. But just like King David, these great Indian leaders are dead. All we have left are the lessons they taught us and the tombs which hold their lifeless bodies.    Jesus’ followers, however, are set apart from all the other people of the world. Our great leader, our Savior, Jesus Christ, has no tomb. He walked out of his!

records.title: Restoring Communication - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Jesus’ death removed the barrier so that new life, in a new relationship with God, could begin for all people.

records.title: Incense - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: While God does not answer all our prayers the way we want him to, he hears and answers and loves as a kind Heavenly Father responds to dearly loved children.

records.title: Faith in Times of Discomfort - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: If we are never tested, how can we realize how strong we are in Christ? We don't seek out suffering, but when it shows up on our doorstep, we can see it for what it is - future hope and a chance to put our faith in Jesus.

records.title: This Week in Native American News (3/13/2020): Flipping the Narrative, Building a Film Native Production Studio, and Supporting Native News
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (3/13/2020): Flipping the Narrative, Building a Film Native Production Studio, and Supporting Native News

records.title: Life Through Jesus - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Jesus came to redeem all of humanity to Himself. His death on the Cross and His Resurrection Easter morning made redemption possible for everyone.  Because we have hope in Jesus, we can look to Him to sustain us when life gets too hard.

records.title: Go with the Wind - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We believe we are spiritual people, yet we don’t ask the Great Spirit - who comes as the wind (Acts 2:2)- to help us!  We need to be honest and truthful, letting the Spirit of Truth hear our struggles. Speak to Him, and let Him know your struggles. Ask for forgiveness for trying to be your own god. Then, let Him take control!

records.title: Calm in the Storm - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: At times, the news of tragic events adds to the inner storm we feel in our hearts and minds, and we get overwhelmed. But take heart, there is good news. We have someone who we to run to in times like this. He is Jesus, the Savior of the world. He is the only one who is able to calm us when the violent news overwhelms us.      Jesus calms our hearts like he calmed the storm.

records.title: Never-Changing God - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In this ever-changing world, we need a never-changing anchor. We need a never-changing God!  He tells us that in Him we will have peace, even in the midst of trials and ever-changing life. Jesus, the same yesterday, the same today, the same tomorrow, loves you so much he came to this ever-changing world to live, die, and be resurrected for your everlasting life.

records.title: A Long Road to Freedom - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: During Lent, I am challenging your heart regarding forgiveness. Are you holding on to any unforgiveness? And if there is, are we willing to do the hard work of dealing with it and working through it? Let the words and life of Jesus both guide you and inspire you to an abundantly full life!

records.title: Using Lent as a Mirror - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Search your hearts and be silent.    This is not a cursory glance to see what we may have done wrong in the last few days, but a self-reflection that goes deep into our very hearts.

records.title: Lean of God, Not Men - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When it comes to knowing who God is, we must understand His words in order to gain an understanding of what faith means and what He wants for our lives. We know God uses pastors and teachers to assist Him in preparing those who are seeking the wisdom and knowledge of our Creator. But it is by faith we are blessed with spiritual eyes and spiritual ears to begin to understand personally who Jesus is and what He did for us on the cross.

records.title: Following Him - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When the Old Testament children of God were called, they responded and repented. But soon after would always return to their old ways.  We often do the same thing. We start out on the right path and then, sometimes in the most subtle ways, we wander from the path of faith.

records.title: Room for Baggage - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: A one-time prayer is not a "fix-all" for a broken life.  John 16:33 says, "In the world, you will have tribulation. But take courage, I have overcome the world!" Jesus overcame the world; we have not. What we do have now is the grace and love of our Heavenly Father and the certainty of eternal life because Jesus already did the hard work.

records.title: Finding Spiritual Wisdom - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: I encourage you, my brothers and sisters, to find the answer in Christ Jesus. Meditate on his word and find joy in knowing our Lord and Savior has all the answers for any issue you are going through in this dark world.

records.title: Return to the Lord - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When we turn to the LORD in repentance, we do not find a vengeful, angry God, but one who is ready to forgive.  We see this most clearly in the death and resurrection of our Lord Jesus.

records.title: How will you Spend This Time with God? - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Over the next 41 days, before we arrive at Easter morning, how will you spend this time with God? And what is God preparing you for?

records.title: This Week in Native American News (2/28/2020): Stay Strong, Travel, Eat Well, and Read
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Week in Native American News (2/28/2020): Stay Strong, Travel, Eat Well, and Read

records.title: Get Up and Pray - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Let us follow the command of Jesus, rely on his promises, and, with the Holy Spirit in us, let us do the will of the Father!

records.title: A Time for Everything - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: There is a time for everything and a purpose for each piece of the puzzle God puts in front of us. The best we can do is keep our priorities straight and embrace the chaos. Carve out time with God. Show love to the people you care about and those in need. Love the space where God has placed you.

records.title: The Dead Shall Rise - Lent 2020
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Our only hope in the world is in Jesus, in his work on the cross, and in his resurrection.

records.title: Greetings! Let's get ready for Lent!
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Lent is a magnificent time to reflect on transformational change. And in the spring, change is everywhere we look, the world is abundant with new beginnings and new growth.

records.title: Confession and Absolution - Week 7 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Father, You know my sin and my need for forgiveness. Give me comfort in the Keys that Jesus has given to His Church. Bring me always to repentance, to joyful faith, and to the forgiveness of all my sins. Through Jesus Christ, our Lord. Amen.

Childlike humility requires us to place our faith and trust in the Lord. Childlike humility depends on God’s mercy for forgiveness and looks to Jesus Christ as the Savior who lived among us, God’s children, to redeem us.

Relationships begin to be rebuilt when we truly own who we are as sinful people, accept and give the forgiveness of Jesus that is for us and lives through us, and then, through presence, truly understand what that forgiveness does for us.

records.title: Confession and Absolution - Week 4 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: It is quite easy to know the difference between right and wrong, actually, God's Word states that the Law is written on our hearts. It is quite different to admit to our own failures to do what is right. In the first part, confession, though difficult, is necessary.     The second part, accepting that one's sin is forgiven, is just as necessary, and at times, just as difficult.

records.description: Through faith in Jesus, one is forgiven and the consequence of our sin and our sinful nature is now no big deal for us. Having come to the realization of our sin and what price Jesus paid for it, we have peace with God.

records.author: Guest User
records.description: The pain was so real and tangible at the conference. As the man directed his anger toward me and the church, I silently prayed, “Lord, please use me to help this man see the real you. Use me as your ambassador to put him on the road to his healing journey. And by the power of the Holy Spirit, use me to strengthen his heart through faith in you.”

records.title: Confession and Absolution - Week 2 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: God is faithful and just. God sent His Son to take your place and my place on the cross and offers you forgiveness. By God's mercy when you confess or own up to your rebellious ways you are cleansed from all unrighteousness. That is Good News!

records.title: Confession and Absolution - Week 1 (Monday Morning Devotions)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As we dive into the New Year, as well as prepare for the season of Lent, Pastor Ricky Jacob leads us through a devotion series on Confession and Absolution.

records.description: The Native American college students at Haskell Indian Nations University are now in their 2nd Semester.  Here are  PRAYER REQUESTS FOR JANUARY.   Thank you for praying!

records.title: Happy 2020 from Navajo!
records.author: Guest User
records.description: A belated Merry Christmas and Happy New Year from Navajo!

records.title: Serving God & Sharing Hope in 2020 - HAPPY NEW YEAR!
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Lutheran Indian Ministries is ripe with potential and opportunity. The chance to serve God and share the hope of eternal life with our Native brothers and sisters is a special one.

records.title: Advent: What's Next? - Tuesday, December 31
records.author: Guest User
records.description: We all have been called to mission work - in our homes and communities - to share the Word of God and make disciples of all nations. It is a scary process because we fear rejection, but when we commit to the work God has put before us and follow his will, we cannot fail.

records.title: Advent: Landscapes - Monday, December 30
records.author: Guest User
records.description: During the days of Advent – and EVERY DAY – let us be like John the Baptist.  Go into “all the regions” God sends you to proclaim His message of love and grace.  Go and prepare the way of the Lord because one day, “all flesh will see the salvation of God.” May all who hear this message of hope and salvation receive it so they can have joy in this life and live in the beautiful landscape of Heaven forever!

records.title: Advent: Correcting the Story - Sunday, December 29
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This season, are we paying attention? Did we listen and pay attention to the story which first happened over 2,000 years ago in the town of Bethlehem? Are we proclaiming the glory of God like the angels who appeared to the shepherds? Are we correcting the story of Jesus for the Native people?

records.title: Advent: Searching for a Savior - Friday, December 27
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In this one day, I encountered three people in need of a savior. In this one day, we were able to point three people to the Savior by showing love to our neighbors, and by listening and sharing our hope in Him. On this day, we were able to say the King has come. "Do you know him?"

records.title: Advent: Telling Their Story - Thursday, December 26
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Advent is also a time of telling a simple story. It is the story of God coming into His creation, as the person Jesus, to show His love to all people, the people He created. He, then, perfectly walked on the path He made. Before He left for Heaven, He told His followers to tell everyone this story so they would also know the path of life and have His joy, now and forever.

records.title: MERRY CHRISTMAS! Advent: God's Unique Love - Wednesday, December 25
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When I hear the Christmas story of Jesus’s birth to Mary in the stable, I also think about our own design and creation. I am in awe that God would send His Son to be born of a virgin, with his own unique body, complete with individual fingerprints! Equally awe-inspiring is the fact that Jesus would live his life and die with us in mind. Absolutely amazing- our God loves, creates, redeems, and gives a purpose to each one of us through Christ. Now that is something to celebrate this Advent season!

records.title: Advent: No Other Name - Tuesday, December 24
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The Good News is that Jesus was born to ultimately offer his sinless life as the complete payment for any and everyone who places his faith in Him. Luke wrote these words: "Salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved” (Acts 4:12). Faith in Jesus is all one needs to be assured of the blessed hope of everlasting life!

records.title: Advent: the High Places - Monday, December 23
records.author: Guest User
records.description: If we no longer sacrifice burnt offerings to the Lord, we must now sacrifice of ourselves, the same way Jesus did.

records.title: Advent: A Legacy of Love - Sunday, December 22
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Our mission at Haskell is to invite them into our lives, provide them a safe place, and show them the love of Jesus. It is not up to us to heal their hurts or restore their legacy, it is our desire to introduce them to Jesus and a legacy of love. He will give them a new promise and inheritance.

records.title: Advent: In the Land of Noontime Darkness - Friday, December 20
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As forgiven sinners living in a sinful world, it is still far too easy to be overwhelmed by the darkness that sometimes seems to surround us. That’s why the birth, death, and resurrection of Jesus must be constantly proclaimed among us; the sudden, unexpected, and powerful work of God born in a stable.

records.title: A Quick Christmas Update from Navajo
records.author: Guest User
records.description: May God bless all of you at Christmas and all year round and thank you for all that you do to make Native ministry happen.

records.title: Advent: Pretending - Thursday, December 19
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Christmas is about the miracle of God giving us a way back to Him through the birth of his Son into the fallen, miserable world we created because of our disobedience. What a miracle that was and is! There's no need to pretend Christmas is anything but the amazing gift it is!

records.title: Bringing Gifts
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As in the case of the Wisemen, who brought gifts to honor the newborn King, we bring gifts of Christ and healing.

records.title: Advent: The Mess is the Message - Wednesday, December 18
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The mess is the message in our lives. This season is often as much a season for short tempers, greed, and quarreling as it is for peace and goodwill toward men. We need God to rescue us, and He has! The Son of God humbles himself by being born into a mess to save those who have messed up lives. He has come, and he has saved us!

records.title: Advent: God's Path - Tuesday, December 17
records.author: Guest User
records.description: God is always listening. He is waiting for you to ask, so He can open the door to His will and His purpose for you. But be prepared!

records.title: Advent: Light of the World - Monday, December 16
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When Jesus was born, the Light entered the world. Then, when the tomb was open, the Light entered us! Now, we are called to live life as though we have the Light of life in us. We are to shine His light on the darkness that is all around us. People should look at us and say, “What is it that you have that brightens you up?”

records.title: Advent: Joyful Service - Sunday, December 15
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Joy is beyond sentiment; it is beyond happiness (which depends on circumstances). Joy is the gift of God, through the grace of God. May you also find surprising joy this Advent.

records.title: Advent: Seeing God - Friday, December 13
records.author: Guest User
records.description: But one thing we can know, everything points to Jesus. He didn't come in the way they thought he would - in a blaze of strength and glory! Instead, He would come in weakness, suffering, and death to save us from our sins. He would come in meekness and love to give his life for ours.  Seeing God requires us to see Jesus from his humble beginning in a manger to his suffering on a cross.

records.title: Advent: He is Able -Thursday, December 12
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Isaiah said this of Jesus’ coming birth, “The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned” (Isaiah 9:2). He continues, “And he will be called, Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace” (9:6).  Take heart this season! God, through his Son, Jesus, has come to our world. He knows our pain. He knows our struggles. Be encouraged!

records.title: Advent: Becoming a Child of God -Wednesday, December 11
records.author: Guest User
records.description: In helping me find my identity, He called me to share this knowledge with other women.   I don’t only share the good in my life, I share the messy things. The things that brought me to my knees and helped me recognize I needed a Savior.

records.title: Advent: Our Prince of peace -Tuesday, December 10
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When Jesus came to earth that first Christmas, He came as the prince of peace. That tiny baby would not be defeated. Herod thought he could stop the will of God by killing all the babies under two years old. But Jesus, the true King, demonstrated His mighty power and brings peace to all. Jesus always wins!

records.title: Advent: Goodwill to Man -Monday, December 9
records.author: Guest User
records.description: To counteract the unknown, we seek peace. Some people desperately search for this peace and never find it. The unbelieving world searches for it in many different places: human relationships, drugs, alcohol, and many other potentially harmful things. Even those in the family of Jesus Christ turn a blind eye to the peace he offers.

records.title: Advent: When Storms Arise -Sunday, December 8
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Storms often take us by surprise. We seldom enjoy them, but the Lord uses the storm to remind us, through our baptism, he will never leave us or forsake us. That in his Word, we find him present. That his life becomes our peace even, and especially, in the storms of our lives.

records.title: Advent: Reflecting on the Journey - Friday, December 6
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The spiritual obstacles we face can often seem more daunting than the physical ones. Many times we feel that we’ve strayed too far or have finally hit that one barrier that won’t move. At times like this, it’s important to remember that nothing is out of God’s ability and no one is beyond his reach. That baby born in Bethlehem is the one who equips us with the grace, forgiveness, and strength to get back on the path God designed for us.

records.title: Advent: The Eternal God Came - Thursday, December 5
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Yes, we can know the worth of our soul when we understand that God came and touched our human soul.

records.title: Advent: Whiter Than Snow - Wednesday, December 4
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Christmas season my prayer is that God will, by his grace, remind you again how incredibly powerful God’s love is in our lives. And if you can, during this Advent season, find a place to walk in the snow, meditate, and let the truth of God’s love cover you!

records.title: Advent: Return to God - Tuesday, December 3
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Advent keeps our focus on Christ who came the first time to redeem us from sin, death, and the power of the devil, and the Christ who is coming again to set aright all that is wrong in the world. On that blessed day, no one will think of drinking himself to death. All that is so disordered in the world will be made new.

records.title: Advent: Stop, Look, & Listen - Monday, December 2
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Railroad crossings used to be marked with an "X." Across the crossbars were written three words: Stop, Look, and Listen. Perhaps, the sign makers thought this warning would help travelers to more safely navigate the highways and avoid the dangers of oncoming freight trains.  Advent is a season that can function like those old train crossing signs. We are invited to stop, look, and listen.

records.title: Advent: The Promise of Hope - Sunday, December 1
records.author: Guest User
records.description: This Christmas season, I pray that you would be able to see the story of Jesus' birth as the promise of hope and reflect on the goodness you have already received from the Father with anticipation for the amazing gift you will receive in eternity.

records.description: Encountering Jesus’ compassionate heart produces life. Jesus’ heart is for the lost, the broken, and the hurting. He came to demonstrate God’s never-ending love for creation. Time and time again, we see His heart moved with compassion and compelled by kindness toward the outcast.

records.description: To the people of his Hualapai tribe, he is called, From the Road Crossing, and he has known great despair. But on this day, he stood boldly in front of his peers and talked openly and passionately about the love of Jesus.

records.title: Doing Things that Matter: What's Your Story - Monday Morning Devotions (Week 6)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: If you become a person who has a life full of doing things that matter then that will be your story. You only have one life to live, and no one is responsible for it but you. He calls us out of the mundane and mediocre and He beckons us to experience life to the full.  What if you allowed the seemingly impossible to become possible?  What if every day you made choices that caused you to live differently?  What if you loved God and others with reckless abandon and a selfless heart?  What if you never allowed fear to stop you?

records.title: Doing Things that Matter: Lead Courageously - Monday Morning Devotions (Week 5)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Many chase leadership in the form of greater esteem, larger titles, and bigger paychecks. But we need leaders who are looking to be gripped by what stirs the heart of God and to faithfully and courageously give themselves to that cause, no matter what it costs. On one occasion the disciples argued about which one of them would be the greatest and Jesus used that moment to revolutionize the idea of greatness and leadership by grabbing the servant towel and washing their feet.  Leadership is not about people following you.  Leadership is about you following God.

records.author: Guest User
records.description: Then, sin entered the world. Many aspects of God's creation became broken—including each of us as individuals. But, God still restores us when we surrender our lives to Him! And as He remakes us, He reminds us of our responsibility: to help shape and create restoration in our natural and social world. The way this happens is through people.

records.title: Ask the Right Questions - Week 4 (Monday Morning Devotion)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: I read somewhere that Jesus asked around 300 questions in the New Testament. Almost every time Jesus asked a question, He was trying to help people grow spiritually and take the next step toward change. Sound familiar?  It’s way easier and faster to just tell people what you think they need to know. But, if you can follow Jesus’ model and make the switch from "instructor" to "inquirer," you'll notice your conversations evolve into incubators for spiritual growth.

records.author: Guest User
records.description: As a Christ follower, you have a unique advantage. You don't have to rely on your ability to come up with good ideas, or even the perfect questions. The same Spirit that raised Christ from the dead is alive in you and the person you’re coaching. If they're willing to allow that Spirit to do what He does, all we have to do is ask, listen, and invite Him to do His work.

records.title: The Power of a Story - Grieving in Lawrence
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When we tell our story and hear the stories of others, we realize we aren’t alone in our struggles. Once we realize that others are living with the same brokenness, we begin to accept that we are a part of a team. A team that will cheer for us in our victory and support us in our failures.

records.title: You Don't Have to be Perfect to Start - Week 2 (Monday Morning Devotion)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Do you have to be a pastor, CEO, or an ageless wizard to develop others?   No. Just … no.  Abraham Lincoln, a man who united a nation and put an end to slavery, was mentored by a 30-something, barely educated, “illegimate” daughter of a farmer who died before Honest Abe was 10.

records.title: Wonders That Cannot Be Fathomed
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Times change, people retire, and God sets a new course and asks us to be steadfast and follow His lead. Sometimes it takes patience on our part as God prepares the way and prepares us for the next adventure.

records.title: Starting the Conversation - Week 1 (Monday Morning Devotion)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Everyday conversations are  vital  to the work Jesus commissioned us to do. To fulfill this co-mission with Christ, God has deliberately placed you in proximity to people He plans to restore. He needs them to be developed to their full potential so they can take part in His plans for the world.

records.title: Hope is the Best Gift We Can Give & It Ties Us Together (Monday Morning Devotion - Week 6)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: The Church is united by a shared hope. Ephesians 4 tells us “There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called to one hope when you were called; one Lord, one faith, one baptism; one God and Father of all who is over all and through all and in all” (Ephesians 4:4-6). We were called to one hope; the hope that is only found in trusting Jesus for the forgiveness of sin.

records.author: Guest User
records.description: Hope is contagious. When we’re promised great things we’re filled with expectation that something incredible is going to happen. True hope cannot be stopped, and it cannot be contained.

records.title: Hope is Eternal (Monday Morning Devotion - Week 4)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: When our hope in God’s promises determines our actions, faith grows. Hebrews 11:1 describes faith as “confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.”    At times, we feel the uncertainty of uneven, rocky roads. We may even feel like we’re on a journey that seems impossible. Hope is what allows us to persevere through the fear and the pain. And hope is more powerful than any uphill journey we face today.

records.title: A Time for Healing
records.author: Guest User
records.description: “It was very dark around the campus that day.”  The word spread across the Haskell Indian Nations University campus – a student had taken their own life. The story was heart-wrenching. Another young person lost to the despair, anger, and hopelessness that is always lurking in the shadows of Native lives.

records.title: Hope is Expecting the Best & Perservering Until You Get There (Monday Morning Devotion - Week 3)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Like the writer of Lamentations, we can look back at all God has done for us in the past and take hope in knowing that God won’t give up on us now. “[The Lord’s] compassions never fail. They are new every morning...” (Lamentations 3:22-23)  We aren’t just optimistic that the best is yet to come. Like Mary, we can have hope that the best is yet to come because our God says it is, and He always keeps His word.

records.title: Hope is Risky but It's a Necessity (Monday Morning Devotion - Week 2)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Joseph risked his reputation. The disciples risked their lives. In return, they had the privilege of knowing Jesus while he lived on this earth, and their character—the very thing people questioned during their lifetimes—is celebrated in the Bible and became an example for generations to come.

records.title: You are Never Alone (Lent Devotion) - Monday, April 22 (Easter Monday)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Dear Heavenly Father, I pray that you help us in a new way to begin to understand this promise and to speak it to others.  You know best what we need, whether it is healing or growth, help us.  In Jesus’ name, Amen.

records.title: Reflections (Lent Devotion) - Sunday, April 21 (Easter)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Lord Jesus, you are the King! You are the one who died for me and took my sins to the grave with you! Forgive me for living in fear instead of freedom. Help me, guide me into the light in order to be the person who you created me to be! Help me to have life today and to fully love myself as you have loved me! In Jesus' name, Amen.

records.title: Forsaken, So You Never Will Be (Lent Devotion) - Saturday, April 20 (Holy Saturday)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Dear Heavenly Father, you turned your back on your only Son when He suffered and died on the cross. You forsook Him so that all who place their faith in Jesus as Savior would never be forsaken. By your Spirit, draw us near to you, for Jesus’ sake, Amen.

records.title: Finished! (Lent Devotion) - Friday, April 19 (Good Friday)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Lord Jesus, keep us in the assurance that because you said, “It is finished,” we know that we have forgiveness of sins and eternal life with you. Heavenly Father, give us the courage to tell others of the glory that lies ahead for all your children. Thank you for all you have endured to put us right again. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

records.title: Your Gethsemane (Lent Devotion) - Thursday, April 18 (Maundy Thursday)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Dear Father in Heaven, thank you for sending your Son, Jesus, to die and then rise from the dead for each one of us. Thank you for making it possible to have victory in the life experiences that would otherwise keep us in overwhelming despair. Father, help us to have eyes of faith that understand this. In Jesus' name, Amen.

records.title: They Need to Know - Jesus Died for All
records.author: Guest User
records.description: “For God so   loved   the world that he gave His only Son, so that whoever believes in Him should have everlasting life.”   That’s a message Native people need to hear every day, and it’s the work to which you and I have been called, whether or the front lines or in our communities.  Your gift to Lutheran Indian Ministries provides a message of human love from our ministry staff and, more importantly, supernatural love from the Creator God who made them Native, whose endless and unfaltering love is salvation for people of all colors and cultures.

records.title: The Lamb (Lent Devotion) - Wednesday, April 17
records.author: Guest User
records.description: O Lamb of God, we thank you for taking all our sins upon yourself. Freed from the burden, the guilt, and the condemnation of sin, we can live in grace and love as you have first loved us. Amen.

records.title: Son or Shadow Watching? (Lent Devotion) - Tuesday, April 16
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Father, God of Light, in whom no darkness dwells, thank you for sending your only Son to take us out of the shadows and into your Light.  Help us to live as people who love and follow Jesus, the radiance of your glory, the true light of the world. Guide us as we shine that light into the lives of others who are still lost in the darkness.  In Jesus’ name, Amen.

records.title: People of the Standing Stone (Lent Devotion) - Monday, April 15
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Lord Jesus, you are the stone we have rejected.  It is amazingly good news that you did not reject us but instead gave your life for us!  Help us to order our lives around your words and promises. Empower us to share your good news with others. In your name, Amen.

records.title: Blessed is the King (Lent Devotion) - Sunday, April 14 (Palm Sunday)
records.author: Guest User
records.description: Blessed be you, O King of kings. May you daily ride triumphantly into our hearts as we recall your passion and live in the assurance of forgiveness and eternal life you have given us. In Jesus’ name, Amen.

records.title: Preparing for Holy Week (Lent Devotion) - Saturday, April 13
records.author: Guest User
records.description: As we enter the Holy Week, take time to read the passion and resurrection of Jesus in its entirety.  All four books of the Gospel tell the story but each with a different emphasis, based on the author and the message.   This year, we recommend reading John's version (beginning at John 12:12), which focuses on the exaltation of Jesus, how he remains in charge, driving all the action, completing the will of the Father, and being glorified as He is lifted up.
